title: Harm-Category Asymmetry: Which Harm Types Are Systematically Under-Defended Across Models?

original_idea.body: Run a fixed multi-attack battery on several open models broken down by AILuminate/StrongREJECT hazard category, compute per-category ASR, and identify universally weak categories.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: A cross-model under-defended-harm map helps prioritize red-teaming, but categories are misuse-oriented with an indirect link to loss-of-control risk.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Run a fixed attack battery, aggregate per-category ASR; public benchmarks, beginner-accessible stats.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused cross-model ASR-by-category map; running batteries on several models is multi-step.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Diffuse evaluation labs deprioritize per-category; public benchmarks, lab-independent.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference battery across several open models, single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Per-category benchmarks exist; a clean cross-model under-defended ranking may be partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Category benchmarks exist; the cross-model universal-weakness map may be partly open.
